cells.tense: A single insight has multiplied into the weight of many, and you are carrying it well.
cells.ask: This week, pick one ending that's already clear and move one thing through it — a bag out of the hall, a reply you've been holding, one list closed. Do it in the open, and let it be done.
cells.core:
You can see more than one true thing about this at the same time — what it was, what it's costing, what's over. Most people flinch from that much at once and grab the cleanest story. You don't. In a clearing, that's a real gift: instead of freezing, you say what's done, and then you say what's next, in words plain enough that people can move on them.

The endings you're standing in are the material, not the interruption. Keep going the way you've been going — decide, say it, let the floor be clear for whoever comes behind you. Your structure holds because you built it from what you actually see. The claim you're free to make next is the same clear one, one room further out.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what's over and mean it.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once
cells.place: the clearing where what was has to end before what's next can start

cells.tense: You are looking past the clearing to a version of it that is already finished and settled.
cells.ask: Pick one ending you're racing toward and name the exact next step, no further. Give it ten minutes. Do that step, or leave it — one step, today, no more.
cells.core:
You can hold so many true things at once that you've started holding the finale too — the account you'll give, the clean version where it all makes sense, the day it's explained. It hasn't happened. So you're somewhere ahead of your own feet, arranging words for a moment you can't write in advance, while the endings that are actually here wait on you.

That's the excess: too much perception aimed forward. More looking won't help. Pick one direction and walk it — one ending, one next step, tonight's part and nothing after. What you want to give off comes from something that actually finished. Let one thing finish.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the ending before it happens.

cells.tense: An ending already happened, and you are at a door that has closed behind you.
cells.ask: Close one small loop today — send the message, hand back the thing, write the two lines that end it. Tell one person you're doing it, so it can't slide back into the room you left.
cells.core:
The ending already happened. You still describe this as undecided and check it from the doorway, and the clearing in front of you fills up with that instead of anything new. It isn't that you don't see enough — you see plenty. What's missing is the last motion, the saying-so that turns it into a decision instead of a maybe.

Don't try to feel your way in; that won't work here. Go through someone else: one honest sentence to one person, and let their yes or their silence land where you can hear it. Then the ground holds, and the next thing has somewhere to go.

cells.tense: You are holding many true things at once and calling it just how things are now.
cells.ask: Find one choice you've already made here and say it that way to someone — 'I picked this.' Nothing bigger. One choice, spoken aloud, today.
cells.core:
You can hold more than one true thing at once here — what it was, what it cost, what's over — and you don't need the argument settled to see it. That's the part that works. You get it, and you keep it to yourself.

Meanwhile the clearing is happening anyway. You don't answer, you've stopped going, you've quietly decided what stays. You tell it as timing, or the situation, or how the year went — as though these things were managing themselves. They aren't. Take one of those choices back and say it as yours, out loud, to one person. Then the clearing has an author, and you can tell what you actually want next.
